title: Varaha Avatar: The Boar Who Lifted the Earth
sources: Bhagavata Purana, Canto 3, chapters 13 and 17-19 (the boar from Brahma's nostril, thumb-sized then vast; the Earth lifted from the Garbhodaka ocean on his tusks; the battle with Hiranyaksha)
Vishnu Purana, Book 1, chapter 4 (Varaha raises the Earth and sets her afloat on the waters)

lines.text: Long ago, a demon named Hiranyaksha grew so powerful that nothing could harm him.
lines.caps: LONG *AGO | A *DEMON | NAMED *HIRANYAKSHA | GREW SO *POWERFUL | *NOTHING | COULD *HARM HIM
lines.say: Long ago, a demon named Hirun-yahk-sha grew so powerful that nothing could harm him.

lines.text: He stormed through the three worlds, and even the gods fled before him.
lines.caps: HE *STORMED | THROUGH THE *THREE WORLDS | EVEN THE *GODS | *FLED | BEFORE *HIM

lines.text: Drunk on his own strength, he seized the Earth herself,
lines.caps: *DRUNK | ON HIS OWN *STRENGTH | HE *SEIZED | THE *EARTH HERSELF

lines.text: and dragged her down to the bottom of the cosmic ocean.
lines.caps: AND *DRAGGED HER | DOWN TO THE *BOTTOM | OF THE *COSMIC OCEAN

lines.text: The world went dark, and the gods cried out for help.
lines.caps: THE WORLD WENT *DARK | AND THE *GODS | CRIED OUT | FOR *HELP

lines.text: Without the Earth, there was nowhere left for life to stand.
lines.caps: WITHOUT THE *EARTH | *NOWHERE LEFT | FOR *LIFE | TO *STAND

lines.text: Then, from the breath of Brahma the creator, a tiny boar appeared, no bigger than a thumb.
lines.caps: *THEN | FROM THE *BREATH | OF *BRAHMA | THE *CREATOR | A *TINY BOAR | *APPEARED | NO *BIGGER | THAN A *THUMB
lines.say: Then, from the breath of Bruhma the creator, a tiny boar appeared, no bigger than a thumb.

lines.text: In moments it grew as large as a mountain, and its roar shook the heavens.
lines.caps: IN *MOMENTS | IT *GREW | AS LARGE AS A *MOUNTAIN | AND ITS *ROAR | SHOOK THE *HEAVENS

lines.text: This was Varaha, Vishnu in the form of a mighty boar.
lines.caps: THIS WAS *VARAHA | *VISHNU | IN THE FORM OF | A MIGHTY *BOAR
lines.say: This was Vuh-rah-ha, Vishnu in the form of a mighty boar.

lines.text: He plunged into the dark waters, searching the deep for the lost Earth,
lines.caps: HE *PLUNGED | INTO THE *DARK WATERS | *SEARCHING | THE *DEEP | FOR THE LOST *EARTH

lines.text: and found her resting on the ocean floor, cold and silent.
lines.caps: AND *FOUND HER | *RESTING | ON THE OCEAN *FLOOR | *COLD | AND *SILENT

lines.text: Gently, he lifted her onto his shining tusks.
lines.caps: *GENTLY | HE *LIFTED HER | ONTO HIS | SHINING *TUSKS

lines.text: But Hiranyaksha blocked his path, swinging his mace.
lines.caps: BUT *HIRANYAKSHA | *BLOCKED | HIS *PATH | SWINGING HIS *MACE
lines.say: But Hirun-yahk-sha blocked his path, swinging his mace.

lines.text: They fought a thunderous battle that shook all three worlds,
lines.caps: THEY *FOUGHT | A *THUNDEROUS BATTLE | THAT *SHOOK | ALL *THREE WORLDS

lines.text: until, with one final blow, Varaha struck the demon down.
lines.caps: UNTIL | WITH ONE *FINAL BLOW | *VARAHA | *STRUCK | THE DEMON *DOWN
lines.say: until, with one final blow, Vuh-rah-ha struck the demon down.

lines.text: Then he rose from the sea, the Earth balanced on his tusks,
lines.caps: THEN HE *ROSE | FROM THE *SEA | THE *EARTH | *BALANCED | ON HIS *TUSKS

lines.text: and set her softly back in her place among the stars.
lines.caps: AND SET HER *SOFTLY | BACK IN HER *PLACE | AMONG THE *STARS

lines.text: The Earth goddess, Bhudevi, bowed in thanks.
lines.caps: THE EARTH *GODDESS | *BHUDEVI | BOWED IN *THANKS
lines.say: The Earth goddess, Bhoo-dayvee, bowed in thanks.

lines.text: Forests grew, rivers ran, and life returned.
lines.caps: *FORESTS GREW | *RIVERS RAN | AND *LIFE | *RETURNED

lines.text: This is Varaha, the third avatar of Vishnu,
lines.caps: THIS IS *VARAHA | THE *THIRD | *AVATAR | OF *VISHNU
lines.say: This is Vuh-rah-ha, the third avatar of Vishnu,

lines.text: a reminder that no matter how deep the world sinks, it can always be lifted again.
lines.caps: A *REMINDER | NO MATTER | HOW *DEEP | THE WORLD *SINKS | IT CAN *ALWAYS | BE *LIFTED | *AGAIN
